beats.label: S1 · Ash reawakens the curse
beats.text: Working a dead-end retail job, Ash gets stoned and reads from the Necronomicon during a hookup, unwittingly unleashing the Deadite plague on his town again.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the entire premise: the plague only exists because Ash reopened the book, and every following character is responding to what he restarted.

beats.label: S1 · Two hunters close in
beats.text: State detective Amanda Fisher hunts Ash for the killings, while a mysterious woman named Ruby — who claims she wrote the book — quietly tracks him too.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces both of the season's outside players. Ruby becomes the ongoing antagonist; Amanda becomes the ally whose death anchors the finale.

beats.label: S1 · A team forms
beats.text: Coworkers Pablo and Kelly force Ash to fight after his own neighbor turns; a Deadite wearing Kelly's mother's face soon confirms the horror is already spreading.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the core trio that carries every future season and gives Kelly a personal loss that binds her to the fight.

beats.label: S1 · The Brujo's answer
beats.text: Pablo's shaman uncle gives Ash a vision — he must bury the Necronomicon at the original cabin. The Brujo dies exorcising a demon from a possessed Kelly.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season's destination (the cabin) and hands Pablo the Santa Muerte medallion that begins his own supernatural arc.

beats.label: S1 · Amanda dies at the cabin
beats.text: Amanda finally believes Ash and joins the group. At the cabin, an evil duplicate of Ash impales her on a deer mount before the real Ash can save her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Ash's institutional ally and shows the cabin itself weaponising his own image against him, priming the finale reveal.

beats.label: S1 · Ruby's true face
beats.text: Ruby reveals she wrote the Necronomicon. Rather than destroy it, she rips off its face and fuses it to Pablo, using him to unleash the evil worldwide.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Flips Ruby from cleaner to architect and marks Pablo with the book — the single event that redefines every relationship going forward.

beats.label: S1 · The deal
beats.text: Ash accepts Ruby's truce — she may release the spirits she claims to control if she leaves him alone. He drives to Florida as sinkholes open across the Earth.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the compromise the whole next season detonates. Ash walks away with the world already breaking, on a promise from someone who has lied about everything.

cliffhanger.text: Ash has fled toward retirement in Florida, having bargained with Ruby — the true author of the Necronomicon — to let her release an evil she promises she can control. Sinkholes are already tearing open around the world.
questions: Can Ruby actually control what she's unleashed?
What has she done to Pablo now that the book's face is bonded to him?
How long before Ash is forced to fight again?

characters.name: Ash Williams
characters.line: Aging Deadite fighter reluctantly back in the game after triggering the curse himself; now living on a Florida beach in denial.

characters.name: Pablo Simon Bolivar
characters.line: Loyal coworker and nephew of the Brujo, marked by the Necronomicon — its severed face is now fused to him.

characters.name: Kelly Maxwell
characters.line: Hardened coworker who lost her mother to a Deadite and was briefly possessed by Eligos; fully committed to Ash's fight.

characters.name: Ruby Knowby
characters.line: Revealed as the author of the Necronomicon; brokered a truce with Ash so she could release the evil she claims to command.

characters.name: Amanda Fisher
characters.line: State detective who finally allied with Ash at the cabin and was killed there by his evil duplicate.

beats.label: S2 · Retirement broken
beats.text: Deadites attack Ash's Florida retirement, forcing him and the gang back to his hometown of Elk Grove, where his father Brock openly resents his cowardice.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season in the place Ash spent decades running from and introduces his father, whose approval and death shape everything he does here.

beats.label: S2 · Uneasy alliance with Ruby
beats.text: They find Ruby wounded and hunted by her own demon children. She reveals the real threat is her ex-husband Baal, and grudgingly allies with Ash.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Flips Ruby from villain to ally and names the season's actual antagonist — every subsequent choice hinges on trusting her enough to fight him.

beats.label: S2 · Baal wears skin
beats.text: Baal arrives on Earth killing to wear people's flesh. He can now pose as anyone in the group and turns Elk Grove's own townspeople against Ash.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Baal's core threat — no one in the room can be trusted — which drives the paranoia of every subsequent episode.

beats.label: S2 · Pablo becomes the vessel
beats.text: The spell to banish Baal begins emerging on Pablo's skin. Ruby admits birthing her children cost her immortality, making Pablo their one real shot.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Pablo at the centre of the endgame and forecasts that beating Baal will cost him — the causal setup for his death in the finale run.

beats.label: S2 · Asylum trap, Pablo cut in half
beats.text: Baal traps Ash inside an asylum illusion trying to break him. Ash plays along and springs a trap — but Baal slashes Pablo in half as he is banished.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The banishment costs Pablo his life, which is the sole motive for the time-travel gamble that reshapes the season's ending.

beats.label: S2 · Time travel goes wrong
beats.text: To resurrect Pablo, the gang travels to 1982 to stop young Ash finding the Necronomicon — and lands in a corrupted alternate timeline instead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The alternate timeline is what lets a second Ruby exist to survive the finale, so this beat is the mechanism behind the closing shot.

beats.label: S2 · Hero, with a catch
beats.text: Ash kills Baal, Pablo revives, and Elk Grove hails Ash as a hero — but an alternate Ruby has slipped through, and the Necronomicon is picked up by a stranger.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes Baal, resurrects Pablo, and seeds the two threats — surviving Ruby and the found book — that reopen the story in the next season.

cliffhanger.text: Elk Grove finally reveres Ash as its hero, but an alternate-timeline Ruby watches him from afar and the Necronomicon has been picked up by an unknown traveler at the ruins of the cabin.
questions: What does this surviving Ruby want now that her original was killed?
Who has the book, and how far will they let it spread?
Can Ash actually live as a hero in the town that ran him out?

characters.name: Ash Williams
characters.line: Finally hailed a hero by his hometown after decades of blame; still the only person who knows how to fight the evil.

characters.name: Pablo Simon Bolivar
characters.line: Cut in half by Baal and brought back through the timeline swap; devoted to Ash and increasingly tuned to the supernatural.

characters.name: Kelly Maxwell
characters.line: Hardened field fighter who has grown closest to Ruby-as-ally over the season and lost more of her old life along the way.

characters.name: Ruby Knowby
characters.line: The alternate-timeline Ruby who slipped through the swap and now watches Ash from afar; the original was killed by her past self.

characters.name: Brock Williams
characters.line: Ash's estranged father, killed mid-season by the possessed Delta after finally coming to accept his son.

characters.name: Baal
characters.line: Ruby's ex-husband and a shape-wearing skin demon; banished back to hell by Pablo's spell.

beats.label: S3 · The daughter he never knew
beats.text: Ash learns his former lover Candace bore him a daughter, Brandy. He races to save her from a Deadite ambush, but Candace is decapitated in front of her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the person the whole season is built around; Brandy's grief and distrust of Ash is the emotional axis every antagonist manipulates.

beats.label: S3 · Ruby's mirror-image spawn
beats.text: Ruby impregnates herself with Ash's blood and births a spawn made in his image, planning to use it to poison Brandy against her real father.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the specific weapon Ruby will use on Brandy — a fake Ash — which pays off in the school dance turn against him.

beats.label: S3 · Knights of Sumeria and the Rift
beats.text: An ancient order — the Knights of Sumeria — arrive hunting the book. They reveal that a Rift can be opened to the Deadlands, the realm between our world and Hell.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Rift is the season's central mechanism: it's how Ash later crosses over to retrieve Kelly and Brandy, and how the Dark Ones eventually arrive.

beats.label: S3 · Pablo becomes the Brujo
beats.text: Brandy stabs the possessed Pablo with the Kandarian Dagger; he passes through the afterlife and returns as the new Brujo, spiritually bound to the Necronomicon.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Pablo's new bond to the book is what lets him read the Sumerian text, open the Rift, and see events remotely — every plan hereafter depends on it.

beats.label: S3 · Kelly killed, body hijacked
beats.text: Ruby kills Kelly with the Kandarian Dagger and installs the imprisoned sorceress Kaya inside her body to sabotage Ash from within his own group.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kelly's death drives the Rift rescue in the finale and Kaya-in-Kelly is the traitor inside the group for the final act.

beats.label: S3 · Brandy dies for Ash
beats.text: At the school dance Ruby's Ash-clone terrorises Brandy into doubting her father. When Ruby hurls the dagger at Ash, Brandy leaps in front of it and dies.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Brandy's death is the second body needed to justify Ash crossing the Rift and directly triggers his descent into the Deadlands.

beats.label: S3 · Kandar rises, Ash wakes in the future
beats.text: The Dark Ones claim Ruby's soul and summon Kandar the Destroyer. Ash slays it with the Kandarian Dagger and wakes years later in a postapocalyptic future.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Ruby as an antagonist and delivers the time jump that resets Ash's world and premise — the entire launchpad for anything that comes next.

cliffhanger.text: Ash saved the world by killing Kandar the Destroyer, but woke injured and alone in a postapocalyptic future — met by a stranger named Lexx and a heavily modified Delta 88, with no sign of Brandy, Kelly, or Pablo.
questions: What happened to the world while Ash was out?
Where are Brandy, Kelly, and Pablo now?
Who is Lexx, and why has she come for him?

characters.name: Ash Williams
characters.line: Killed Kandar with the Kandarian Dagger and woke in a wrecked future with a new augmented right hand.

characters.name: Brandy
characters.line: Ash's daughter; died at the school dance protecting him, was brought back through the Rift, and evacuated with the survivors.

characters.name: Kelly Maxwell
characters.line: Killed by Ruby and revived through the Rift; survives the finale evacuation, though her body was briefly worn by the sorceress Kaya.

characters.name: Pablo Simon Bolivar
characters.line: The new Brujo, spiritually bound to the Necronomicon and able to see through its eyes; survived the finale.

characters.name: Ruby Knowby
characters.line: The alternate-timeline Ruby; scheming with Kaya until the Dark Ones arrived and claimed both their souls.

characters.name: The Dark Ones
characters.line: Ancient masters of the Necronomicon who reclaimed the book and summoned Kandar the Destroyer before Ash cut him down.

characters.name: Lexx
characters.line: Augmented woman from the postapocalyptic future who found the injured Ash and is now driving him out to explain what has happened.
